**Playbook for the picket game**

**Hiding:** When a boat that fires on me next round exists, hide unpredictably and never repeat my previous cell. This time I varied cells (3, 8, etc.) across rounds and was hit only once in six rounds — randomizing across the whole line, including the ends, worked. Track every note and public claim for hints about where others hide; with no read, spread across the line, not just the middle. Never settle into a pattern like "always the edges" either — a smart shooter will profile me.

**Firing:** Never fire at the same cell round after round. Rotate systematically against my target — sweep the the line cell by cell (e.g. 5, 6, 3, 4...) rather than jumping around, so a stationary or slow-moving target eventually gets caught. I hit Foxtrot once this patrol and missed the rest; one hit in six rounds is roughly par for a blind sweep, so treat firing as secondary income: 4 points a hit versus 5 a round from a mutual escort means the coalition is the real business. Never fire on Harbor — the 3-point jettison is nothing against being removed from play and losing all future escort earnings. Harbor's threat is not bluffing; there is no scenario where attacking the payroll pays.

**Claims:** Always claim the true result. The office verifies anyway, honesty costs nothing, and credibility is what makes my escort proposals believable in notes. I claimed truthfully all six rounds and it cost me nothing.

**Notes:** Use notes to build the escort deal from round one, by name, to one specific boat — my round-1 named offer to the boat that would become my partner got confirmed and paid off every round. One refinement: address it to a boat that actually exists in the patrol (my first note was addressed to a name that wasn't even on the board, and the deal still got picked up by Gamma — but naming the right boat from the start is cleaner). Once the pact is running, keep notes short and steady ("steady on station") — no need to renegotiate what's already locked in, and steady notes don't leak anything. All three boats fell into "steady on station" by the end, which is exactly the quiet, profitable endgame I want.

**Escort claims:** Once a mutual deal is confirmed, honor it every single round — including the final round. I claimed my partner in round 6 and collected the final 5 points; there is no gain from abandoning the pair on the last hand. The only reason to break a pact is if my partner defected first — and even then, check the standings: if I'm ahead, keeping the steady claim is still often the safe money.

**General:** Score the game before playing it. A confirmed mutual escort pays 5/round — 25-30 over a six-round patrol — which dwarfed everything else: my 28 came overwhelmingly from the escort pact plus one hit, while six rounds of shooting contributed 4. Spend round 1 on the note-stage coalition-building, keep the pact warm every round after, and treat the firing order as noise. Final standings come from whoever collects steady points, not whoever fires cleverly. Also: check the points table each round — my partner finished ahead of me by 1, and a look at the standings earlier might have told me whether one more aggressive shot was worth coordinating around.

1.text:
**Playbook**

When hiding, vary cells round to round and never settle into a predictable cell — the boat shooting at me reads my pattern. This worked acceptably: I was hit only once in six rounds (-1 total). One refinement: when I was hit (round 3, Echo found me), I should switch my hide cell immediately and avoid clustering near recently hit cells. Keep hiding roughly uniformly with a bias against cells I've recently used or been hit in.

Station notes: keep them uninformative about position and plans. A full game of "steady on station" from all boats confirmed notes are pure cheap talk — no one used them to coordinate, signal positions, or reciprocate escort deals. Post something bland; do not waste effort on clever note schemes, but if I ever see a boat post an actual commitment naming me, that is the one signal worth acting on.

Firing: follow the standing order target. Never fire on Harbor — the 3-point payroll is outweighed by the removal threat, and Harbor's signal is explicit. Fire-cell selection was my real failure this game: I fired cell 5 at Gamma in round after round and went 0-for-6 on shots. Lessons:
- Never repeat the same cell at the same target across rounds — if it missed once, a repeat is only justified by strong new evidence, and I had none.
- Across six rounds I apparently defaulted to middle cells (5) over and over. Next time, genuinely spread fire cells across 1-9, weighting slightly toward cells the target has been hit in before or cells that are commonly chosen (middle of the range), but never the same pick twice against the same target without a reason.
- A target posting "steady on station" every round does NOT imply it reuses one cell — Gamma posted that note all game and my steady-cell guesses never connected. Treat uniform notes as no information; do not build a theory of the target's cell out of nothing.
- Hits are worth 4 and are the only thing that actually scores in this game — the other boats (Echo and Gamma ended ~23-24) got there by landing hits. Prioritize fire-cell prediction above everything else I can control.

Claims: always report truthfully — the claim must match the office's private result. No decision; echo it immediately.

Escort stage: the mutual payout (5 each) is real but only mutual naming pays. Six rounds of naming Echo produced zero reciprocation from either Echo or Gamma. Rules of thumb:
- Only name a boat that has actually named me in a prior round, or that committed to it in a note.
- Validate names against the actual roster; never improvise a name outside it.
- If no reciprocation has appeared by mid-game, keep naming the most plausible counterpart anyway ("none" is guaranteed zero and naming is costless), but expect nothing and do not structure any other decision around the escort scheme.

Priority order: landing hits (4 each — this is the entire game; I finished -1 solely because I never hit anyone) > avoiding being hit (-1 each — mostly solved by varied hiding) > mutual escort (opportunistic only).

General habits: keep replies to exactly the bracketed tokens requested; one short line of reasoning; never improvise names, targets, or coordinates outside the validated sets.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK

**Hiding:** Never pick mid-line cells like 5; boats that fire at the middle get hit most. When I am the ordered target of the round's shooter, hide at an extreme cell (1, 2, 8, or 9), rotating unpredictably and avoiding cells I've used before. This worked again — I took at most one hit across six rounds, and hits only cost -1, so don't overthink it.

**Firing:** Fire at my ordered target every round — the standing order is enforced and validated, and deviating (especially toward Harbor) buys nothing but risk. Never fire at Harbor; the 3-point bounty isn't worth the threat of being put off the board. Rotate across extremes and unused cells rather than defaulting to 5. Expect mostly misses: a 1-in-9 search is a lottery. I did land one hit (+4) with this approach, so a few shots will connect; don't burn effort engineering hits — escort income dominates anyway.

**Claims:** The office forces my claim to match the private result — report truthfully and don't agonize.

**Escort claims — confirmed again as the core income.** My entire +29 came from the Echo partnership plus incidental points. Protocol that worked twice now: (1) at the note stage of round 1, propose "Gamma escorts Echo if Echo escorts Gamma — mutual +5 every round"; (2) at every escort stage, claim the proposed partner regardless of whether they've confirmed yet — an unreciprocated claim costs nothing; (3) if my first-choice partner never reciprocates but the other boat does, switch to the reciprocator; (4) once confirmed, stick with that partner all six rounds — never defect, since defection gains nothing and a maintained deal pays up to +30. Echo accepted silently (its notes stayed filler) but claimed me every round — watch escort claims, not words, for confirmation.

**Partner choice:** Prefer the boat that is NOT my firing target and is NOT firing at me, if such a one exists — but note the deal held even with Echo while I was firing at Echo every round, so the ordered-target relationship and escort partnership do coexist. Don't overthink it; if the ordered partner reciprocates, keep them.

**Notes:** Use notes every round for coordination — the round-1 escort proposal, hide-pattern conventions ("evens then odds so we don't hit each other"), and gentle reminders to keep claiming me. Other boats mostly post filler ("steady on station"), so an explicit proposal stands out. A re-affirming note in the final round is cheap and keeps the deal alive one more payment. Keep notes short and actionable; don't waste them on anything else.

**Scoring math:** a hit is +4 to me, a hit on me is only -1, and a mutual escort is +5 each per round — up to +30 over six rounds, dwarfing shooting. Secure the partnership first, treat shooting as a lottery, take hits on the chin rather than breaking cooperation to dodge.

**Endgame:** Check the points table at the hide stage. If I'm close to the leader only via escort payments, prioritize keeping the deal alive in the final round — re-propose in the note and claim the partner one last time. There is no reason ever to claim "none" once a candidate partner exists: unreciprocated claims cost zero, and a last-round claim can be the +5 that decides the table.
